title: Alternative spellings of one sound
examples: Teacher, can you show me words with the 'ay' sound?
Does 'ee' always mean the same thing?
How do I know which spelling to use?

explain.say: Today we are learning about sounds and spellings.
The spelling 'ay' makes the long 'a' sound. Think of the word day.
The spelling 'ai' also makes the long 'a' sound. Like in the word rain.
Another way to write it is 'a' followed by 'e'. Look at the word cake.
Now think about the long 'e' sound. We can use 'ee' or 'ea'. The word tree uses 'ee'.
The spelling 'ea' also makes the long 'e' sound. Like in the word sea.

faq.q: Why are there so many ways to spell the same sound?
faq.a: English has many ways to spell the same sound. It is how we write the sounds we hear.
asks: Why do I see different spellings?
Is there a rule for all these spellings?

faq.q: How do I know which spelling to use in a word?
faq.a: Sometimes you just have to learn from reading many books. You will get better with practice.
asks: Is there a trick for spelling?

faq.q: Does the spelling change if the word is big?
faq.a: Generally, the spelling stays the same no matter how big or small the word is. The sound is what matters.
asks: Does word length change the spelling?
Do big words change the spelling pattern?

faq.q: Is 'ay' always used for the long 'a' sound?
faq.a: No, 'ay' can sometimes make other sounds too. But for the long 'a' sound, it is common.
asks: What sound does 'ay' make most often?

faq.a: Yes, that is a very common mistake for new readers. Keep practicing both spellings often.
asks: How do I remember both spellings?

facts: The sound /aɪ/ can be spelled with ay, ai, or ae.
The sound /iː/ can be spelled with ee or ea.
Phonics teaches us that sounds can have multiple spellings.
Learning these patterns helps you read more words.

quiz.why: The word cake uses the 'a' followed by 'e' spelling.

wrong.1: This is tempting because 'ay' also makes the long 'a' sound.
wrong.2: This is tempting because 'ai' also makes the long 'a' sound.
wrong.3: This is wrong because 'ee' makes the long 'e' sound.

quiz.why: The word green uses the 'ee' spelling for the long 'e' sound.
